info.name: Bifrost V1 - Request Guards
info.description: Hermetic wire-contract tests for the management and gateway surface's request guards, run against the shared e2e gateway with dashboard auth disabled and no live provider. Each folder pins what the server refuses over the API and that nothing was persisted as a side effect: file:// and unreachable catalog URLs on PUT /api/config, MCP client registrations with an unsupported connection_type or a loopback/unresolvable target, proxy / provider / provider-key endpoint changes that need an admin session, the OAuth2 issuance endpoints while mcp_server_auth_mode is headers, malformed passthrough paths and unknown x-model-provider values, a zstd body declaring an oversized window, the on-demand test delivery of a private-network webhook, and auth_config updates that must prove the stored admin password. The last folder only runs when the runner sets admin_exists=1 (a stored admin account whose password is admin_password); it re-enables auth and disables it again, so the gateway ends in the state the following suites expect. There is no collection-level 2xx gate: every request asserts its exact status with the response body in the message.

item.name: Catalog URL validation
item.description: PUT /api/config refuses file:// values for pricing_url, model_parameters_url and mcp_library_url (those are config.json-only), reports an unreachable http URL with one fixed message, and persists none of them. If a guard regresses and a rejected URL is stored, a skip-gated PUT restores the three earlier catalog URLs.

item.name: A double slash after the prefix is answered by the gateway

request.description: fasthttp collapses duplicate slashes before routing, so the handler sees a rooted remainder (/127.0.0.1:1/x) and the explicit double-slash rule is a second layer. What this case pins is that the request is still answered 400 by the gateway, either by the path rule or by the provider lookup, and never forwarded: sgl is a known provider that no e2e profile configures (it takes a key-level URL), so there is no upstream to reach.
